title: Universal incidence commutes with changing the base scheme
statement: Given f:Y→Spec k, i:X→Y, an invertible module L on Y and finitely many global sections sᵢ, tensor pullback of their universal incidence equation defines the incidence scheme over X. Its canonical map to the incidence scheme over Y forms a cartesian square over i. It preserves the coefficient projection. The pullback unit preserves scalar multiplication and local free-generator coefficients, and an affine-local generator pulls back to a global generator when the entire source maps into that affine open.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, proof; tensor-pullback and affine-coordinate details

proof.text: Compare tensor pullback along a composite with iterated tensor pullback. The comparison identifies pulled-back sections and scalar multiplication, hence identifies the two incidence ideal sheaves. Restrict the canonical ambient product pullback square to the closed subschemes; equality of the pulled-back ideal gives the cartesian incidence square and the projection formula. Apply the same tensor comparison to a local free generator to obtain its coefficient formula.

theorem isPullback_bertiniIncidenceBaseChange
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (u : X ⟶ Y) (L : Y.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    {I : Type u} [Fintype I] (s : I → Γ(L, ⊤)) :
    IsPullback (bertiniIncidenceBaseChange f u L s)
      ((bertiniUniversalIdeal (u ≫ f) ((tensorPullback u).obj L)
        (fun i ↦ tensorSectionsUnit u L (s i))).subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd _ _)
      ((bertiniUniversalIdeal f L s).subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd _ _) u
